notes: The M3-2 full report supersedes the M3-1 advance (durable-goods-2026-09-25) for the same August 2026 reference month, seven days later — the modal gap. This edition's identity is its morning, not its content: 2026-10-02 is the September Employment Situation (BLS's own schedule page, fetched direct; tracked `high` jobs-2026-10-02, 8:30 a.m.), and this print lands 90 minutes later. That collision is what this ledger measures, and it decomposes a lean both twins reported. The M3-2-day SPY range excess (1.106% vs a 0.961% baseline) is a COMPOSITION EFFECT of the 11 payrolls-day editions in the class: strip them and M3-2 days run 1.076% at permutation p=0.215 — indistinguishable from an ordinary session — while the payrolls-day editions run 1.365% at p=0.051. The Atlanta Fed agrees at the model level: GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx carries NO PostedUpdates row for 2026-10-02 (posted rows either side are 10-01 "Construction spending, ISM Manufacturing Index" and 10-06 "International trade (Full report)"), and its InternalUpdates row for the date reads "M3-2 Manufacturing (Full report), Employment situation" — jointly attributed. So m3-full-report-2026-12-03's kill switch, which named 2026-10-02 and 2026-11-03 as its next two candidate M3-2-alone vintages, is now dead on BOTH (the November twin retired 11-03; this retires 10-02 on two independent grounds).
